outcomeNote: a single homiletic exposition of the name Reuben with five prooftexts; no challenge is raised

segments.he: רְאוּבֵן. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אָמְרָה לֵאָה: רְאוּ מָה בֵּין בְּנִי לְבֶן חָמִי. דְּאִילּוּ בֶּן חָמִי, אַף עַל גַּב דְּמִדַּעְתֵּיהּ זַבְּנַיהּ לִבְכֵירוּתֵיהּ, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּמְכֹּר אֶת בְּכֹרָתוֹ לְיַעֲקֹב״, חֲזוֹ מָה כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ: ״וַיִּשְׂטֹם עֵשָׂו אֶת יַעֲקֹב״.
segments.en: Tangential to the mention of Leah’s son, Judah, and the reason for his name, the Gemara explains the sources for other names, including «Reuben. Rabbi Elazar said:» Reuben’s name should be considered a prophecy by Leah, as «Leah said: See [re’u] the difference between my son [beni] and the son of my father-in-law,» Esau, son of Isaac. «Even though» Esau «knowingly sold his birthright» to his brother Jacob, «as it is written: “And he sold his birthright to Jacob”» (Genesis 25:33), nonetheless, «behold what is written» about «him: “And Esau hated Jacob”» (Genesis 27:41).

segments.he: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיֹּאמֶר הֲכִי קָרָא שְׁמוֹ יַעֲקֹב וַיַּעְקְבֵנִי זֶה פַעֲמַיִם״ וְגוֹ׳.
segments.en: Esau was not only angry over Isaac’s blessing, but he was angry about another matter as well, «as it is written: “And he said, ‘Is he not rightly named Jacob, for he has supplanted me twice?» He took my birthright, and behold, now he has taken my blessing’” (Genesis 27:36). Despite having sold his birthright, he refused to relinquish it.

segments.he: וְאִילּוּ בְּנִי, אַף עַל גַּב דְּעַל כֻּרְחֵיהּ שַׁקְלֵיהּ יוֹסֵף לִבְכֵירוּתֵיהּ מִנֵּיהּ, דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבְחַלְּלוֹ יְצוּעֵי אָבִיו נִתְּנָה בְּכֹרָתוֹ לִבְנֵי יוֹסֵף״, אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי — לָא אִקַּנֵּא בֵּיהּ, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּשְׁמַע רְאוּבֵן וַיַּצִּלֵהוּ מִיָּדָם״.
segments.en: «While my son,» Reuben, «even though Joseph took his birthright from him by force, as it is written:» “And the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel, for he was the firstborn; «but, since he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph,» son of Israel” (I Chronicles 5:1). «Nevertheless, he was not jealous of him, as it is written» when Joseph’s brothers sought to kill him: «“And Reuben heard and he saved him from their hands,» saying ‘Let us not take his life’” (Genesis 37:21).

R' Elazar: Leah said 'see the difference between my son and my father-in-law's son' — Esau sold his birthright knowingly
moves.about: Esau knowingly sold his birthright to Jacob

moves.summary: Gen 25:33 shows Esau sold the birthright
Gen 27:41 shows Esau nonetheless hated Jacob
Gen 27:36 shows Esau's grievance included the birthright he had sold
moves.about: Esau still counted the sold birthright as stolen from him

moves.summary: the other limb of the contrast: Reuben lost his birthright to Joseph by force, yet was not jealous of him
moves.about: Reuben's birthright was taken from him by force and given to Joseph
